newsitem.title: USA: AlliedSignal to build plant, double output.
newsitem.headline: AlliedSignal to build plant, double output.

text.p: AlliedSignal Inc said Monday it will build a plant that will double production of its high-strength Spectra Fiber and Spectra Shield composites.
The company said the plant is scheduled to begin operations in the third quarter of 1997, with about half of its capacity in production. It will be in full-scale operation about a year later.
Spectra Fiber is used in making police and military body armor, lightweight composites for blast containment, fishing line, cut-protective gloves and industrial slings.
Spectra Shield, which uses the fiber in a patented composite, is used for police and military armor that protects against high-velocity, multi-hit automatic weapons, among other things.
AlliedSignal makes Spectra Fiber in Colonial Heights, south of Richmond, Va. and Spectra Shield in Petersburg, Va.
Company officials were not available to confirm the location of the new plant, its cost or its production capacity.

"The new facility is a response to the escalating worldwide demand for the fiber," it said. "The plant will have the capability of converting all or any portion of that fiber production into Spectra Shield."
